variants.hypothesis: Performance: content-visibility: auto on each row, so selecting a row restyles a screenful rather than all 200 rows.
Hierarchy and fidelity: the title on its own line at the row's full width, with the status moved to the overline's right end, so titles stop truncating at half width.

verdicts.reasons: The two versions differ in one way: how wide the title is on three-line rows (Needs you and Working). In A the title runs the full width of the row under the meta line. B cuts it off at the left edge of the status column, so short titles get truncated next to empty space. In default-1280, streaming-1280 and error-1280, B shows 'Which staging databa…' and 'Fix the billing worker's double c…' where A shows the whole title. The long-content story shows it most: B cuts titles as short as 'Session 2: tidy the rele…' and 'Session 18: tidy the re…', while A shows them in full and only truncates the long 'Re-run the migration…' titles. Since the title is what a person needs to read, A has the stronger hierarchy and is closer to T3's sidebar, where titles truncate at the full row width. B's dead space beside the title also costs it on states and cost. The mobile-420 story looks the same in both, but in default-420 B still truncates 'Which staging databa…' and 'Fix the billing worker's double c…'. Group headers, status colours, Done rows, error notices and copy are the same in both.

The two versions differ in one place: the title line of the three-line rows. In A the title uses the full row width, so 'Which staging database for the dry run?' and 'Fix the billing worker's double charges' show whole in the default, streaming and error stories. In B the title stops at the left edge of the status label above it, even though the title line has nothing to its right, so those titles become 'Which staging databa…' and 'Fix the billing worker's double c…'. The title is the most important thing in a row, so B cuts it for no reason, which hurts hierarchy and moves it away from T3's sidebar, where titles use the full row. In the long-content story, B cuts even short titles like 'Session 2: tidy the rele…' and 'Session 18: tidy the re…' in the Needs you group, while A only cuts the genuinely long 'Re-run the migration…' titles. The default-420 shots show the same early truncation in B, and the dedicated mobile story is identical in both. Spacing, status colours, group headers, the error notices, single-line settled rows and copy are pixel-identical, so those criteria score the same.

The one real difference is how wide the title line is in the three-line rows. In A the title uses the full row width. In B it is cut off at the width of the project/branch part of the meta line above, so it stops well before the status column. In default-1280, A shows 'Which staging database for the dry run?' and 'Fix the billing worker's double charges' in full, while B cuts them to 'Which staging databa…' and 'Fix the billing worker's double c…' with empty space to the right. Long-content-1280 makes this worse in B: short titles like 'Session 2: tidy the rele…' and 'Session 18: tidy the re…' get cut off under 'harbour' rows that have no branch, even though half the row is empty, and A shows them in full. The same thing happens in default-420, streaming-1280 and the stale list in error-1280. That hurts hierarchy, because the title is what you read first, and it hurts long content. The mobile-420 story, the one-line Done rows, the error notices, status colours, spacing and copy look the same in both versions.
